promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What type of circulatory system do mammals such as humans have?
questions.explain: Mammals have a double circulation in which blood passes through the heart twice for each complete circuit of the body.

questions.q: In a double circulatory system, how many times does the blood pass through the heart during one complete circuit of the body?
questions.explain: In double circulation blood passes through the heart twice per circuit: once to the lungs and once to the rest of the body.

questions.q: Which part of the circulation carries blood between the heart and the lungs?
questions.explain: The pulmonary circulation carries blood from the heart to the lungs and back again.

questions.q: A student examines blood inside the pulmonary artery. What is the oxygenation state of this blood?
options: A mixture of oxygenated and deoxygenated in equal amounts
questions.explain: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs to be oxygenated.

questions.q: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.explain: The heart has four chambers: two atria and two ventricles.

questions.q: Which chamber of the heart has the thickest muscular wall?
questions.explain: The left ventricle has the thickest muscular wall because it pumps blood to the whole body.

questions.q: Why does the left ventricle have a thicker muscular wall than the right ventricle?
options: It pumps blood only to the lungs
It pumps blood at high pressure around the whole body
It receives blood from the veins
questions.explain: The thicker muscular wall of the left ventricle generates the high pressure needed to pump blood around the entire body.

questions.q: Which blood vessels supply the heart muscle itself with oxygenated blood?
questions.explain: The coronary arteries branch from the aorta and supply the heart muscle with oxygenated blood.

questions.q: What is the function of the valves within the heart?
options: To prevent the backflow of blood
To add oxygen to the blood
questions.explain: Heart valves ensure blood flows in one direction only by preventing it from flowing backwards.

questions.q: During vigorous exercise a person's heart rate increases. What is the main benefit of this?
options: It cools the body down directly
It delivers oxygen and glucose to muscles more quickly and removes carbon dioxide faster
It reduces the amount of blood in the body
It stops the muscles from respiring
questions.explain: A faster heart rate increases blood flow, supplying muscles with more oxygen and glucose for respiration and removing waste carbon dioxide more rapidly.

questions.q: A patient has a leaky semilunar valve between the left ventricle and the aorta. What is the likely consequence?
options: Blood flows backwards into the ventricle
The heart stops producing red blood cells
The atria enlarge to store blood
questions.explain: A leaky valve cannot prevent backflow, so blood leaks back into the ventricle, reducing the efficiency of circulation.

questions.q: Which type of blood vessel carries blood away from the heart?
questions.explain: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, usually at high pressure.

questions.q: Why do arteries have thick, muscular and elastic walls?
options: To allow substances to diffuse through easily
To withstand and maintain the high pressure of blood pumped from the heart
To slow blood down for exchange
questions.explain: The thick elastic and muscular walls of arteries withstand and help maintain the high pressure of blood leaving the heart.

questions.q: Why do veins contain valves whereas arteries generally do not?
options: Veins carry blood at low pressure and valves prevent backflow
Valves add oxygen to venous blood
Veins have thicker walls than arteries
questions.explain: Blood in veins is under low pressure, so valves are needed to prevent it flowing backwards.

questions.q: What is the main function of capillaries?
options: To pump blood around the body
To exchange substances between the blood and body tissues
questions.explain: Capillaries have walls one cell thick, allowing exchange of substances such as oxygen, glucose and carbon dioxide between blood and tissues.

questions.q: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs back to the heart?
questions.explain: The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium of the heart.

questions.q: Which component of the blood is responsible for transporting oxygen?
questions.explain: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which binds oxygen and transports it around the body.

questions.q: Red blood cells are biconcave and have no nucleus. How does this help their function?
options: It allows them to divide rapidly
It provides more room for haemoglobin and a larger surface area for oxygen absorption
It helps them clot the blood
questions.explain: Lacking a nucleus leaves more space for haemoglobin, and the biconcave shape increases surface area for efficient oxygen uptake.

questions.q: Which component of the blood is mainly involved in clotting?
questions.explain: Platelets are cell fragments that help the blood to clot at wounds.

questions.q: What is the role of phagocytes in the blood?
options: They engulf and destroy pathogens by phagocytosis
questions.explain: Phagocytes are white blood cells that engulf and digest pathogens to protect the body against infection.
